name: sre

findings.message: cycle_dispatch_stage emits stage.start for every cycle member at every iteration in ALL runs (not only resume), because the guard is `_cd_iter > 0` with no `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE` check; the design document for this issue explicitly names this as Gap 7 and states it is NOT YET FIXED, requiring the guard `if [[ ${_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE:-false} == true ]] && [[ "$_cd_iter" -gt 0 ]]; then`.
findings.quote:
if [[ "$_cd_iter" -gt 0 ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "stage.start" "stage=$_cd_stage" \
                || { local _r=$?; warn "eb_emit_event stage.start failed (rc=$_r, continuing — disk/perm/lock?)"; true; }
        fi

findings.message: _runner_resume_rehydrate silently returns 0 when _artifact_persist_restore fails — no log line and no event are emitted — so an operator cannot distinguish a successful resume from one that ran with absent artifacts; the stale-artifact check downstream only fires for stages that have a manifest-declared primary artifact, leaving stages with no primary artifact path silently unprotected.

_runner_from_stage_preflight swallows _artifact_persist_restore failure with `|| true`, making a git-backend failure (network down, branch absent) indistinguishable from 'artifact was never committed'; both paths produce the same 'has no restorable primary artifact' diagnostic, which will mislead an operator diagnosing a git infrastructure failure as a missing prior-run artifact.

The auto-resume via latest symlink branch calls `readlink -f` to resolve the per-run state directory; if readlink fails (broken symlink, macOS without GNU coreutils), state_dir is set to an empty string and all subsequent artifact and state-file operations use paths under an empty prefix, which silently corrupts or misroutes them rather than failing closed with a diagnostic.

_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE is set to false inside _cycle_orchestrator_run_body to prevent nested cycles from restoring their iter; however, if `get_state_field` fails (jq absent, state file corrupt), `_persisted_iter` falls back to 0 via the `|| echo 0` path, _start_iter resolves to 1, and the cycle silently starts from the beginning — the same as a fresh run — with no warning or event that the persisted iter could not be read.
